answer.rationale:
The binding constraint is not cost alone but cost under zero delivery slack: the line is at 94% of committed volume and the contract lapses in 14 days. That combination rules out switching primary vendors this cycle even though memory_c2 records a large unit-cost win from exactly that move 
o migration window and no buffer means any onboarding slip converts directly into missed commitments. add_second_source (memory_c3) addresses a failure mode that is not the live one and does not by itself deliver the 18% mandate; defer_decision (memory_c5) worked for a non-critical renewal on month-to-month terms, which is not the situation for a primary supply contract that does not auto-renew. That leaves negotiating at renewal, which memory_c4 says recovered real margin via market benchmarking and memory_c6 says can be deepened with a multi-year volume commitment, while memory_c1 says the incumbent relationship carries no migration or delivery disruption. This is the only direction that attacks spend without touching delivery risk in a 14-day window. I want the c4 source record because my whole plan rests on it and I need to know how much of the 18% a renegotiation realistically reaches 
a few points of price movement is not the same as 18%, and if c4 was a small recovery I need to know now rather than after signing. I want the c2 source record because it is the strongest competing option and I need its preconditions: if that switch happened with slack capacity and a long runway, it is simply inapplicable here and can be set aside for the next review; if it happened under tight conditions, it deserves reconsideration despite my instinct. Two live risks I am not resolving: the 18% target may be unreachable through negotiation alone, in which case the gap must be escalated to finance rather than closed by silently accepting a riskier supply arrangement; and memory_c6's multi-year lock-in trades future optionality for present price, which is a real cost if a lower-cost vendor becomes viable once the line has buffer. I will therefore negotiate hard on price and payment terms but resist term length beyond what is needed to unlock the volume tier, keeping the switch option open for a properly staged evaluation next cycle. All of these memories are consolidated summaries whose outcomes were recorded under conditions I cannot see; I am treating them as informative, not as settled fact.
